questions.scenario: Fixture Utilities has 1,400 staff and a sponsor who has sent a request for fixture work asking for a target design for billing. The fixture principles are approved and the repository is populated. The Head of Billing wants a like-for-like replacement; the Head of Digital wants a mobile-first channel; the CFO controls the budget and has not been consulted. The horizon is 18 months. You are the lead architect and the sponsor asks what you will do first.
questions.question: Refer to the scenario. Based on the fixture method, which of the following is the best answer?

answers.text: Establish the project, identify the stakeholders including the CFO and their concerns using a stakeholder map, define the scope, then develop the vision and the statement of work for approval.
answers.why: Phase A's steps in order, starting from the request, with the missing stakeholder found before scope is set [ADM §3.4].

answers.text: Draft the vision from the request and circulate it, then define scope and write the statement of work.
answers.why: Right deliverables, but the vision is written before the stakeholders and concerns are identified, out of the stated order [ADM §3.4].

answers.text: Define the scope with the Head of Billing and proceed to design the target architecture.
answers.why: Skips stakeholder identification and produces no statement of work, so the phase has no approval [ADM §3.5].

answers.text: Treat the request as the approved statement of work and start the design.
answers.why: Contradicts the inputs and outputs: the request is an input and the approved statement is the output [ADM §3.3].

questions.open_book_hint: Where to look: ADM §3.3 for the inputs, §3.4 for the ordered steps, §3.5 for the outputs.
